**What happened**
- **Pitch 78** (the 20-day mean-reversion rule, long-only, top 4 of M00–M19, rebalanced every 10 days) failed two gates:
  - Deflated Sharpe: 0.10 against a 0.95 threshold.
  - Capacity: about $0.71M against a $1M minimum.
  - Rank IC (0.10) and correlation (−0.01) passed.
- **Earlier pitches 23 and 47** on the same family failed the deflated-Sharpe gate too. Pitch 23 was close to passing its IC gate and showed a 1.57 Sharpe in its holdout window, but the penalty from the 11 attempts now outweighs that.
- **Library:** empty, so no lessons from prior PMs.

**Assessment**
The mean-reversion effect looks real in 2022–2024 (IC around 0.08–0.12 across windows). The problem is that the holdout Sharpe varies a lot between windows, and the deflation penalty is harsh after this many attempts. I would not expect another variant of the same rule to clear the gate.

**Next step**
Pod-2 is due to be judged on 2024-10-01 and will be let go unless it earns a seed. I'd rather spend the remaining budget on one well-motivated change than on more parameter sweeps. The obvious candidate is a higher-capacity version (more names or a larger universe) to address the capacity gate, but that needs a universe the data allows. I'll leave that decision for the next session.

You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

Its holdout Sharpe was -0.32, so the deflated Sharpe came out at 0.02 against a 0.95 threshold. Capacity also failed, with edge at zero. The same signal looked strong in earlier pitches (Sharpe 1.57 and 2.39 on earlier holdout windows), so it has decayed or was overfit to those windows.

**Why I'm not pitching again:** Pod 2 has used 17 attempts, and each one raises the deflation penalty. The pitch variants I could still try (top_n, rebalance frequency) are the same idea with the same sample, so they would mostly be more tries on the same data. Adding more of them would make the deflated Sharpe worse, not better.

**Other things I checked:**
- Adding a second universe (T00–T19) turned the signal strongly negative (IC -0.28), so the effect doesn't carry over to other names.
- Momentum and low-vol lost money in this universe, per earlier research.

**Status:** Pod 2 has no seed. Under the generation law, my PM seat will likely be let go at the 2024-10-01 month-end unless a future pitch is eligible. The pod-3 closure (library lesson 1) came from a momentum pitch that was eligible but then lost 14% in 16 days, so a passing gate alone is not enough to survive the ladder.

You are the newly hired portfolio manager of a new pod, in the place of a pod that ended (its PM was let go, or the risk ladder closed it). Its lesson is in your input (post_mortem). The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

You are the newly hired portfolio manager of a new pod, in the place of a pod that ended (its PM was let go, or the risk ladder closed it). Its lesson is in your input (post_mortem). The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you.
